usage: 수업 = class; how you'd refer to a studio session
use 하다, not 운동하다; 요가하다 is also fine spoken
매트 is the standard loanword; you'll see it everywhere
-원 suffix marks a small studio/academy (cf. 학원)
examples: 저는 일주일에 두 번 요가를 해요.
I do yoga twice a week.
일주일에 N 번 = N times a week, the natural frequency pattern
요가하면 몸이 진짜 유연해져요.
Doing yoga really makes your body flexible.
유연하다 = flexible; common reason people give
회사 근처에 요가원이 새로 생겼어요.
A yoga studio newly opened near my work.
생기다 = (a place) opens/appears, very common for new shops
nuance: Everyday loanword; everyone says 요가, never a Korean translation. Pair it with 하다 (요가를 하다 / 요가하다) rather than 운동하다. A studio is a 요가원 or 요가 스튜디오, and a single session is 요가 수업 or 요가 클래스.
mistakes: Saying 요가 운동해요 — redundant; just 요가 해요
Calling the studio 요가집 — it's 요가원 or 요가 스튜디오

usage: verb is 하다; 필테 is the texting abbreviation
등록하다 = register; classes are sold in packages
read as 일대일; private lessons are common and pricey
examples: 요즘 자세 교정하려고 필라테스 다녀요.
I'm doing Pilates these days to fix my posture.
다니다 = attend regularly; the verb for going to a gym/academy
필라테스는 요가보다 좀 더 힘들어요.
Pilates is a bit harder than yoga.
N보다 = than N; honest comparison locals make
10회권 끊었는데 벌써 다 썼어요.
I bought a 10-session pass and already used it all.
N회권 = N-session ticket; 끊다 = to buy (a pass)
nuance: Spelled 필라테스 and abbreviated 필테 in chat. Very popular with 20-30s women in Korea, often sold as session packages (회권). Distinguish 기구 필라테스 (machines/reformer) from 매트 필라테스; people will ask which you mean.
mistakes: Writing 필테스 or 파일라테스 — the correct form is 필라테스
Using 사다 for buying a pass — locals say 회권 끊다

usage: 하다 is the verb; also 클라이밍 가다
실내 = indoor; most city climbing is indoor gyms
the short-wall, no-rope style; the most common type
examples: 주말마다 친구랑 클라이밍 하러 가요.
I go climbing with a friend every weekend.
N마다 = every N; -하러 가다 = go in order to do
처음엔 손에 힘이 하나도 없었어요.
At first I had no grip strength at all.
힘이 없다 = to have no strength; what every beginner says
클라이밍장에 암벽화 빌려주는 데 있어요?
Is there a place that rents climbing shoes at the gym?
암벽화 = climbing shoes; 빌려주다 = to lend/rent out
nuance: Said as 클라이밍; the trendy gym version most 20-30s do is 볼더링 (bouldering) at an indoor 클라이밍장. Climbing shoes are 암벽화 and grip chalk is 초크 — useful at the counter.
mistakes: Misspelling it 클라밍 by dropping the 이 — keep it 클라이밍
Confusing 등산 (hiking a mountain) with 클라이밍 (sport climbing on walls)

usage: use 치다 (to strike), like other ball games
게임 is the counter for a round
-화 = shoes; you rent these at the counter
examples: 우리 이따가 볼링 치러 갈래?
Want to go bowling later?
이따가 = later today; -ㄹ래? casual invitation
볼링 한 게임에 얼마예요?
How much is one game of bowling?
N에 얼마예요 = how much per N; counter pricing question
저 볼링 진짜 못 쳐요.
I'm really bad at bowling.
못 + verb = can't do well; humble self-deprecation
nuance: Take the verb 치다 (볼링을 치다), the same verb used for ball/racket sports, never 하다 in careful speech. A 볼링장 is a classic group outing and 회식 alternative. You rent 볼링화 and pay per 게임.
mistakes: Saying 볼링을 하다 — natural Korean is 볼링을 치다
Forgetting you must rent 볼링화 — street shoes aren't allowed on the lane

usage: verb is 치다, like other cue/ball games
-장 = venue; very common, often open late
the version with pockets; 당구 often means 3-cushion
게임 = round; loser usually pays the table fee
examples: 오빠들이랑 당구 치러 갔어요.
I went to play billiards with the guys.
-(이)랑 = with (casual); -하러 가다 = go to do
당구장은 보통 시간당으로 계산해요.
Billiard halls usually charge by the hour.
시간당 = per hour; 계산하다 = to bill/pay
저는 당구 칠 줄 몰라요.
I don't know how to play billiards.
V-ㄹ 줄 모르다 = not know how to do something
nuance: Use 치다 (당구를 치다). A 당구장 is a cheap, late-night hangout, traditionally male-coded but increasingly mixed. Plain 당구 usually means the carom games (사구 four-ball or 쓰리쿠션 three-cushion) played on a pocketless table; the pocketed version is 포켓볼. Halls charge 시간당 (per hour), and the loser often pays.
mistakes: Saying 당구를 하다 instead of 당구를 치다
Assuming 당구 = pool with pockets — that's 포켓볼; plain 당구 usually means a pocketless carom game (사구/쓰리쿠션)

usage: pay-per-hour cafe stocked with games; very common
룰 = rules; staff often explains the game for you
examples: 비 오는 날엔 보드게임 카페 가는 게 최고예요.
On rainy days, going to a board game cafe is the best.
-는 게 최고다 = doing X is the best; natural recommendation
이 보드게임 룰이 좀 복잡해요.
The rules of this board game are a bit complicated.
복잡하다 = complicated; common complaint
넷이서 할 수 있는 보드게임 추천해 주세요.
Please recommend a board game for four people.
넷이서 = with four people; 추천하다 = to recommend
nuance: Said 보드게임, with verb 하다. The cultural anchor is the 보드게임 카페 (often shortened 보드카페), where you pay by time and staff teach the 룰. A popular cheap date or group activity for 20-30s, especially on rainy days.
mistakes: Calling it 보드 게임판 — the game itself is just 보드게임
Using 보다 for playing a game — games take 하다, not 보다

usage: the full venue name; often shortened to 방탈
each scenario room is a 테마; you pick one
쓰다 = to use; staff give hints when you're stuck
examples: 우리 이번 주말에 방탈출 하러 갈까?
Shall we go do an escape room this weekend?
-ㄹ까? = shall we?; soft suggestion to a friend
이 테마 너무 어려워서 결국 탈출 못 했어요.
This room was so hard we couldn't escape in the end.
결국 = in the end; 탈출하다 = to escape
공포 테마는 무서워서 못 하겠어요.
I can't do horror themes because they're scary.
V-겠다 here = I (don't think I) can; reluctance
nuance: Spelled 방탈출 (literally 'room escape'), commonly shortened to 방탈. The venue is a 방탈출 카페, and each scenario is a 테마 you book in advance. You can request 힌트 when stuck; horror ones are 공포 테마. A staple group activity for young adults.
mistakes: Writing 방 탈출 with a space in the activity name — it's the set noun 방탈출
Saying 방탈출을 보다 — you 하다 (do) an escape room, not watch it

usage: verb is 보다, like other performances
예매 = advance ticketing, vs 예약 for reservations
배우 = actor; fans follow specific performers
examples: 대학로에서 뮤지컬 한 편 봤어요.
I saw a musical in Daehangno.
대학로 = Seoul's theater district; 한 편 = one (work)
주말 공연은 표가 금방 매진돼요.
Weekend shows sell out quickly.
매진되다 = to sell out; 금방 = quickly/soon
이 뮤지컬 누가 나와요?
Who's performing in this musical?
나오다 = to appear/be cast; asking about the cast
nuance: Said 뮤지컬, watched with 보다. Korea has a huge musical scene centered on 대학로 (Daehangno) and big theaters; fans pick shows by the 뮤지컬 배우 in the cast. Buy tickets with 예매하다 (advance ticketing), and popular dates 매진되다 (sell out) fast.
mistakes: Using 예약하다 (reserve) for show tickets — performances use 예매하다
Confusing 뮤지컬 (sung-through theater) with 연극 (a straight play)

usage: the standard phrase for the outing
verb is 보다, like other things you view
-전 is the suffix for a themed show
관람료 = viewing fee; some shows are free (무료)
examples: 주말에 친구랑 사진 전시회 보러 갔어요.
I went to see a photo exhibition with a friend on the weekend.
-하러 가다 = go in order to; popular low-key date
이 전시회는 무료라서 사람이 엄청 많아요.
This exhibition is free, so there are tons of people.
무료 = free of charge; 엄청 = a ton (casual intensifier)
전시회 도슨트 시간이 몇 시예요?
What time is the exhibition docent tour?
도슨트 = docent/guided tour; 몇 시 = what time
nuance: A 전시회 is a (usually temporary) exhibition you 보러 가다 — a go-to casual outing or date for 20-30s, especially popular as 사진전 or 미술전. Note the distinct -전 / -회 forms. Watch the 관람료, look for 무료 (free) shows, and many offer a 도슨트 guided tour.
mistakes: Confusing 전시회 (a temporary exhibition event) with 미술관 (the museum building itself)
Using 입장료 loosely — for art shows the fee is usually called 관람료

usage: to go to a karaoke room
pay-per-song booth; 코노 for short, popular and cheap
곡 = counter for songs; 부르다 = to sing
the free minutes staff add at the end
examples: 2차로 노래방 가자!
Let's go to karaoke for round two!
2차 = the next stop on a night out; classic after dinner/drinks
요즘은 혼자 코노 가서 스트레스 풀어요.
These days I go to coin karaoke alone to de-stress.
스트레스(를) 풀다 = to relieve stress; 코노 = 코인 노래방
서비스 시간 좀 넣어 주세요!
Please add some bonus time!
넣다 = to put in/add; what you call out to staff
nuance: A 노래방 is core Korean nightlife — the classic 2차 (second round) after dinner or drinks. The cheap solo-friendly version is 코인 노래방 (코노). Songs are counted with 곡, and you can beg staff for 서비스 시간 (free extra minutes). Distinct from a karaoke bar.
mistakes: Calling it 가라오케 — in Korea the room is a 노래방; 가라오케 sounds dated or refers to a hostess bar
Using 하다 for singing a song — you 부르다 (sing) a 곡

usage: the standard phrase for the outing
the matching shirt-and-shorts set they hand you
the signature snack-bar drink, paired with 삶은 계란
수면 = sleep; you can stay overnight in many
examples: 주말에 찜질방 가서 푹 쉬었어요.
I went to a jjimjilbang on the weekend and rested deeply.
푹 쉬다 = to rest fully/deeply; the whole point of going
찜질방에서 양머리 수건 만들 줄 알아요?
Do you know how to make the 'sheep-head' towel?
양머리 = the rolled-towel hat; V-ㄹ 줄 알다 = know how to
밤새 찜질방에서 자도 돼요?
Is it okay to sleep at the jjimjilbang all night?
밤새 = all night; V-아/어도 돼요? = is it okay to?
nuance: A 찜질방 is a 24-hour Korean sauna/spa where you wear a 찜질복, sweat in heated 한증막 rooms, and can sleep overnight in a 수면실. The iconic experience is the 양머리 towel and 식혜 with 삶은 계란. A cheap, very Korean way to relax or even crash for the night.
mistakes: Confusing 찜질방 (heated communal sauna complex) with 목욕탕 (plain public bathhouse)
Wearing your own clothes in the common areas — you change into the provided 찜질복

usage: any hobby + 동호회 names an adult interest group
정기 = regular/scheduled; clubs meet on a set day
회비 = the fee members chip in for the group
examples: 등산 동호회에 가입해서 사람 많이 사귀었어요.
I joined a hiking club and made a lot of friends.
사귀다 = to make/befriend; a top reason people join
동호회 회비가 한 달에 만 원이에요.
The club dues are 10,000 won a month.
한 달에 = per month; 회비 framed as monthly cost
이 동호회는 직장인들이 많아요.
This club has a lot of working professionals.
직장인 = office worker/professional; common club demographic
nuance: A 동호회 is an adult hobby/interest club (sports, photography, etc.) — the main way 20-30s residents meet people outside work and school. You 가입하다 (join), pay 회비 (dues), and attend the 정기 모임. Slightly more organized and lasting than a one-off 모임; a college version is the 동아리.
mistakes: Using 동아리 for an adult club — 동아리 is a school/university circle; adults join a 동호회
Saying 동호회를 들어가다 literally — the natural verb is 가입하다
